title: Violin-derived tone, no record collection, solos used in schools
summary: Royal's alto sound comes from his violin expression, he avoids records to avoid imitating, and schools now use his solos as teaching material.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Coleman Hawkins and the great saxophonists

blocks.x: alto saxophone
You turned to (inaudible) group because of the commercial demand --
That's right.
How about that creamy tone you get? did you develop that?
-- (inaudible) beautiful thing (inaudible). At what point (inaudible)?
I always played that way because -- always, because that's my violin expression that I do on saxophone. That's the way I played violin. I used to play gypsy violin.
So it's a violin your saxophone.
(Inaudible) influence in (inaudible)?
Yes, I learned how to play with a sensuous

feeling, playing a violin, so I tried to just transpose that into my saxophone playing and that's the way I lead sections and so forth when I play. I never use saxophone players as my guides and I never really like to -- I never collect records. I don't have a record collection, anything of that, because if I continuously listen to somebody else's playing, well, then I'll find myself mimicking them because I'm too easy to pick up on things and I want to be my own self. So, I won't allow myself to even have a record collection.
That's interesting. I've heard that too, that said by a few other people, (inaudible) because even unconsciously, (inaudible) someone else's music will come out-- or sound.

Yeah, unconsciously will end up -- right. So, the type of playing that I play -- I was one of the beginners of that way of playing, so that's mine. So, I don't want it mixed up with anybody else's. I feel proud enough to think that I'm as good as anybody else. So, I'm going to remain for the last few remaining years of my life, as me.
You have a very identifiable and very beautiful sound.

Well, it's gotten to the place now where people can realize that it's me around the corner if they should hear it. As a matter of fact, through many of our higher places of learning, schools like North Texas State, Auburn University and places like that that have good stage bands,

they used to use my solos as part of their curriculum in their teachings and have their little boys sitting down there, playing them, learning how to play like me, so that they can take all of my jobs --
(Laughter.)
-- and starve me to death.
(Laughter.)
They ought to start out and learn the violin first and find out where it came from.
(Inaudible)

It's very amusing to me. I've actually had the experience of having people say, "I looked all over town last week to try to find someone to make a record that sounded like you." When all he had to do was call my house and get me from in front of that damn television tube and I could have come out and been me. I think that takes a lot of nerve.
I do, too. I do, too.

But it's funny. It's all a part of life and I'm at the place now where in a few more years, I will be past the stage where they can starve me to death because I'll be probably drawing social security or something and I won't have to worry about going out, looking for those jobs, and I can laugh at the whole thing.
